text:
ashwin: Quick Q — for SLO notify fallback weighting: should we bias towards lower-cost model/region when a tenant burns high usage? thinking about routing decisions between hosted/dedicated and smaller model variants. sketch below.

tess: I'm +1 for cost-awareness but we shouldn't use raw usage alone. prefer weighting by error_budget_consumption + cost_score. otherwise noisy tenants get cheap models and we lose fidelity.

maria: agree with tess. We also need a telemetry signal for quality regressions (e.g., eval false positive / degraded recall) so we can detect when fallback hurts.

keith: how do we compute "cost_score"? simple tokens * price? we should avoid punishing latency sensitive routes. maybe factor in latency_slo_violation_rate.

samir: proposal: weight = alpha * normalized(remaining_error_budget) + beta * normalized(cost_per_token) + gamma * tenant_priority. defaults: alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=0.1. normalize in [0,1] per-tenant history window=30d.

ashwin: thanks. operational question — do we expose alpha/beta as per-tenant overrides in the console? maybe in the SLO card -> routing section so customers (or ops) can tune?

tess: Console UX: surface an "impact preview" — estimated monthly spend delta + expected regression probability for the tenant if weights change. tiny sparkline and a toggle for preview vs live.

maria: telemetry needs: notify.fallback.count by weight_bucket, notify.quality.delta by tenant, and periodic sampled raw responses (1/1000) tagged with pre/post-fallback to audit quality.

keith: ops wise we must log each fallback decision to trace with a reason tag. example log line: `fallback_decision={"tenant":"acme","reason":"cost","weight":0.32,"chosen":"hosted-small"}`. make sure it isn't PII.

samir: config snippet (proto/JSON-ish) for API consumer: ```json
{"fallback_policy":"weighted","alpha":0.6,"beta":0.3,"gamma":0.1,"buckets":[{"name":"hosted-small","max_cost":0.01},{"name":"hosted-medium","max_cost":0.05},{"name":"dedicated","min_priority":0.8}]}
```

ashwin: rollout plan idea: start with 5% of tenants (only tenants >10k monthly tokens), ramp 5% per week, watch notify.quality.delta and latency_p95.

tess: :thumbsup: Can we add a per-tenant canary toggle in console so SRE/Product can flip fallback on/off for a single org during trial?

maria: add alert rule: if notify.quality.delta > 0.05 for >1h after a fallback change => auto-rollback + page oncall. Also chart a 72h window post-change.

keith: also add a manual override field `force_fallback=false` for Dedicated tenants (they opt-out of fallback routing).

ashwin: I'll draft the API changes and a small Console patch. cc @deploy-bot to create infra job and schedule staging canary.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created issue INF-2481 and scheduled canary run in staging for 2024-07-10 (job id: job-8932).

ashwin: thanks — will post an RFC draft in #eng-platform by EOD.

(tiny followups expected: - add metric tags for weight_bucket, - ensure sampling rate is configurable, - include rollback playbook snippet in runbook)
